posts.title: THE Apple M-Series: Which One Do You Actually Need?
posts.content:
On November 10, 2020, Apple made an announcement that shook the PC world, and since then, things have never been the same. Prior to this announcement, Apple had relied on Intel for the processors that powered its MacBook lineup; the laptops were initially powered by Nvidia graphics cards and later AMD, with many of the budget options getting slightly boosted versions of Intel’s integrated graphics units.

Well, Apple announced the Apple M1 chip in November 2020, and in so doing, they started a revolution that has significantly influenced the market and may have inspired the recently released ARM-based Snapdragon Elite processors for Windows PC (but this is a story for another day, we promise you).

The Apple M processor lineup combines raw power with class-leading and unprecedented levels of efficiency—the MacBook can run for hours without needing to be plugged in. There is virtually no performance difference between when it is plugged in or running on battery, making it great for power users who like to be on the move.

It's been over three years since THAT announcement and the M series is now in its third iteration (not counting the “Pro,” “Max,” and “Ultra” versions). If you are considering getting a new PC and trying to decide on which MacBook to get, we've got you covered. Come closer!

The Value Champion: M1

The M1 may be the first generation, but it's still a powerhouse for everyday tasks.  If you primarily use your MacBook for browsing, email, basic photo editing, or streaming, the M1 offers fantastic performance at a more affordable price.  You'll also find M1 MacBooks in a wider range of models, including the MacBook Air and the entry-level MacBook Pro.

M1 Perfect for:

  • Students and casual users
  • Web browsing, email, and document editing
  • Basic photo editing and streaming

Looking for More Muscle? M2

The M2 steps up the game with a performance boost, particularly for graphics-intensive tasks.  Content creators who do light video editing, gamers who play moderately demanding titles, and coders who work with complex projects will appreciate the extra power. The M2 is also available in a wider variety of configurations, allowing you to tailor RAM and storage to your needs.

M2 Perfect for:

  • Content creators (light video editing)
  • Gamers (moderately demanding titles)
  • Coders (complex projects)
  • Users who want a future-proof option

The Cutting Edge: M3

The M3 boasts the latest and greatest in Apple silicon.  If you're a professional video editor working with demanding 4K or 8K footage, a 3D artist rendering complex models, or a musician running large sample libraries, the M3 offers the most power and efficiency.  Keep in mind, the M3 currently comes at a premium price and is only available in select MacBook Pro models.

M3 Perfect for:

  • Professional video editors (4K/8K editing)
  • 3D artists and animators
  • Musicians (large sample libraries)
  • Developers working on demanding projects

These are summarised overview of each lineup but whichever one you decide to get, rest assured, you are getting Apple engineering at its finest. If you already have any Apple devices, including the iPhone, Apple Watch, Apple AirPods, etc., the MacBook offers some ecosystem benefits that will further enhance your experience.

posts.title: Peace of Mind on Your Wrist: Unveiling the Life-Saving Features of the Apple Watch
posts.content:
When Apple released the OG Apple Watch in 2015, many pessimists were convinced that the device was a fad and with time, it would fade into obscurity. They couldn’t have been wrong. The Apple Watch was a hit when it launched. And in 2024, it has remained an unquantifiable success. For many critics (coughs Samsung fans), it has become a fashion statement rather than an actual fitness device. But that is one of Apple’s superpowers, create a device that appeals to people’s fashion sense yet remains supremely functional. However, beyond being an accessory for making fashion statements, the Apple Watch can SAVE YOUR LIFE! Yes, you read that right!

When was the last time you visited the hospital for even the most basic check-up? Crickets? Yes! That’s what we thought! Now, the Apple Watch (and other health wearables) can not take the place of proper medical checkups, but it will give you on-the-spot feedback before things get really bad, especially during emergencies. Here are 4 ways the Apple Watch can save your life:

  • Heart Rate Monitoring

Your Apple Watch continuously monitors your heart rate and can alert you if it detects irregularities, such as atrial fibrillation (AFib) or unusually high or low heart rates. Early detection of these conditions can prompt you to seek medical attention before they become serious. When you consider the high number of young people with no prior medical issues that just drop dead, you will understand why having a device that monitors your heart for irregularities is a no brainer in 2024.

  • Crash Detection

The latest Apple Watch models (Apple Watch Series 8, Apple Watch Series 9, Apple Watch SE (2nd Generation) and the Apple Watch Ultra) come equipped with crash detection, which can identify severe car accidents. If a crash is detected, the watch will automatically call emergency services and provide them with your location. This feature ensures that help is on the way even if you’re unable to call for it yourself.

  • Blood Oxygen Monitoring

The Apple Watch Series 6 and later models include a blood oxygen sensor that measures the oxygen saturation of your blood2. This feature can help detect respiratory issues early, allowing you to seek medical attention promptly. It’s particularly useful for monitoring conditions like sleep apnea or respiratory infections.

  • Noise Monitoring

Exposure to loud environments can damage your hearing over time. The Noise app on the Apple Watch monitors the noise levels around you and notifies you if the decibel level reaches a point that could harm your hearing. This feature is particularly useful in workplaces with high noise levels, concerts, or any situation where prolonged exposure to loud sounds is common. By alerting you to hazardous noise levels, the Apple Watch helps protect your long-term hearing health.

Beyond our list, the Apple Watch is an incredible tool for gym enthusiasts, it can help you record your sets and reps, track your progress and even come with a platform for competing with your friends. Would you like to get the Apple Watch or any other smartwatch? Send us a DM on Instagram

posts.title: iPad Generations Explained: Your Guide to Choosing the Best iPad
posts.content:
The iPad has changed how we work, learn and have fun. Since its launch in 2010, Apple has kept making them better, with new models and features every year. But with so many options, how do you know which iPad is perfect for you?

In this guide, we’ll delve into the fascinating world of iPad generations, unravelling the differences between each model to help you make an informed decision. It’s important to note that the generations of iPads follow the size of the tablet, meaning each size category has its own unique progression of generations. Let’s explore how these generations are organized based on their size and identify major design changes.

The Classic iPad: The Versatile All-Rounder

The original iPad, launched in 2010, has been steadily improving. It's a fantastic option for everyday tasks such as browsing the web, watching videos, reading e-books, and even light creative work. Here's how it's evolved over the years:

  • 1st Generation (2010): Introduced the revolutionary tablet concept with a 9.7-inch display.
  • 2nd Generation (2011): Added a dual-core A5 chip for snappier performance and cameras for FaceTime calls.
  • 3rd Generation (2012): Boasted a stunning Retina display and the powerful A5X chip for smoother multitasking.
  • 4th Generation (2012): Introduced the Lightning connector (still used today) and the even faster A6X chip. Notice how there's a JUMP from 2012 to 2017 in the iPad release dates. The gap is due to Apple's strategic decision to focus on the iPad Air line during that period.
  • 5th Generation (2017): Made a comeback with improved performance and a more budget-friendly price.
  • 6th Generation (2018): Added support for the Apple Pencil, opening up new creative possibilities for drawing and note-taking.
  • 7th Generation (2019): Increased the screen size to 10.2 inches for more immersive viewing and included a Smart Connector for attaching keyboards.
  • 8th Generation (2020): Upgraded to the A12 Bionic chip for a significant performance boost across apps and games.
  • 9th Generation (2021): Featured the A13 Bionic chip and an improved front-facing camera for sharper video calls and selfies.
  • 10th Generation (2022): Received a sleek redesign with a larger 10.9-inch display, the A14 Bionic chip for even faster performance, and a convenient USB-C port for versatile connectivity.

When do you think apple will release the 11th Gen?. Let us know in the comments!

The iPad mini (Power in Your Pocket)

If you prioritize portability without sacrificing performance, the iPad mini is your perfect companion. Here's a look at its evolution:

  • 1st Generation (2012): Introduced a smaller 7.9-inch display for ultimate portability while maintaining iPad functionality.
  • 2nd Generation (2013): Upgraded to a Retina display and the A7 chip for a smoother, more visually pleasing experience.
  • 3rd Generation (2014): Added Touch ID for secure login and payments, adding convenience and peace of mind.
  • 4th Generation (2015): Featured the A8 chip and improved cameras for better photos and videos.
  • 5th Generation (2019): Brought Apple Pencil support and the A12 Bionic chip, turning the iPad mini into a portable creative powerhouse.
  • 6th Generation (2021): A major redesign with an edge-to-edge display, the lightning-fast A15 Bionic chip, and USB-C for faster charging and versatile connectivity. This is the latest iPad mini

Do you think we could see the iPad mini 7 soon?

The iPad Air (The Perfect Balance of Power and Portability)

Striking a sweet spot between the standard iPad and the powerhouse iPad Pro, the iPad Air delivers impressive performance in a lightweight package. Let's see how it's progressed:

  • 1st Generation (2013): Introduced a lighter, thinner design compared to the standard iPad, making it more comfortable to hold and carry.
  • 2nd Generation (2014): Added a laminated display for reduced glare and improved image quality, along with the powerful A8X chip for seamless multitasking.
  • 3rd Generation (2019): Made a triumphant return with a 10.5-inch display and the A12 Bionic chip, offering a blend of performance and portability.
  • 4th Generation (2020): Redesigned with an edge-to-edge display for a modern look, with the A14 Bionic chip for impressive speed, and USB-C for flexible connectivity.
  • 5th Generation (2022): Took a significant leap forward with the M1 chip (the same powerhouse found in MacBooks), 5G support for lightning-fast internet on the go and improved cameras for stunning photos and videos.
  • 6th Generation (2024): This latest iPad Air model brings two size options: 11-inch and 13-inch. It is powered by the M2 chip for desktop-level performance and features an upgraded front-facing camera that is optimized for landscape use, perfect for video calls. The larger model also boasts landscape stereo speakers with spatial audio for an immersive entertainment experience. This was just released

The iPad Pro (The Ultimate Creative and Professional Powerhouse)

The iPad Pro is the pinnacle of iPad technology, designed for professionals, artists, and anyone who demands the absolute best. It comes in two sizes:

11-inch iPad Pro

  • 1st Generation (2018): Introduced an edge-to-edge display for an immersive viewing experience, Face ID for secure login and Apple Pay, and the A12X Bionic chip for unparalleled performance.
  • 2nd Generation (2020): Featured the A12Z Bionic chip for even more processing power and a LiDAR scanner for enhanced augmented reality experiences and precise depth sensing.
  • 3rd Generation (2021): Took a massive leap forward with the M1 chip, bringing desktop-class performance to a tablet, and 5G support for ultra-fast internet connectivity.
  • 4th Generation (2022): Upgraded to the even faster M2 chip, becoming the fastest iPad ever
  • 5th Generation (2024): This latest 11-inch iPad Pro model brings the powerhouse M4 chip, offering up to 1.5x faster CPU performance than the M2, making it ideal for demanding tasks like video editing and 3D design. The new chip also enables an all-new display engine for the Liquid Retina XDR display, providing stunning visuals with incredible brightness and contrast. The upgraded front-facing camera, optimized for landscape use, makes it perfect for video calls. This is the latest 11" iPad Pro.

12.9-inch iPad Pro

  • 1st Generation (2015): Introduced a massive 12.9-inch display aimed at professionals who need a larger canvas for their work.
  • 2nd Generation (2017): Featured a brighter display for improved visibility a better camera and the A10X Fusion chip for a significant performance boost. 
  • 3rd Generation (2018): Introduction of Face ID for secure and convenient device unlocking, and the A12X Bionic chip for exceptional speed and power.
  • 4th Generation (2020): Included the A12Z Bionic chip and an extra camera module and a LiDAR scanner for cutting-edge augmented reality capabilities.
  • 5th Generation (2021): Introduced the M1 chip and a stunning mini-LED display with incredible brightness and contrast for a truly immersive viewing experience. 
  • 6th Generation (2022): Upgraded to the M2 chip, further enhancing its performance and making it a powerhouse for demanding tasks.

Which iPad Is Right For You?

The best iPad for you depends entirely on your individual needs and budget. Consider what you'll primarily use it for, how important portability is to you, and how much power you need.

Whether you're a casual user, a student, an artist, or a professional, Apple has an iPad that's tailor-made for you. You can shop for an iPad from us by clicking here.

posts.title: Apple Watch Series 8 vs. Apple Watch SE 2: A Detailed Comparison
posts.content:
The Apple Watch Series 8 and the Apple Watch SE 2 were both released on the same date, September 16, 2022. Despite sharing a release date, these two models cater to different audiences, with varying features, capabilities, and price points. In this blog, we will delve into the key differences between the Apple Watch Series 8 and the Apple Watch SE 2 to help you decide which one suits your needs better.

1. Design and Display

  • Apple Watch Series 8: The Series 8 continues the premium design tradition, featuring an always-on Retina display. It comes in 41mm and 45mm case sizes, offering a larger display area that curves towards the edges, making it easier to read notifications and interact with apps. The Series 8 also offers a more durable display with crack-resistant front glass, IP6X dust resistance, and swim-proof capabilities (WR50 rating).
  • Apple Watch SE 2: The SE 2, while maintaining a sleek design, offers a more budget-friendly approach. It has a Retina display but lacks the always-on functionality, which means the display turns off when not in use. The SE 2 comes in 40mm and 44mm case sizes. Although it has a durable design, it doesn’t offer the crack-resistant front glass or the IP6X dust resistance that the Series 8 does.

2. Health and Fitness Features

  • Apple Watch Series 8: This model is packed with advanced health features. It includes the new temperature sensor that enables cycle tracking, advanced sleep monitoring, and even crash detection. The Series 8 also includes the ECG app, blood oxygen monitoring, and an array of workout modes, making it a comprehensive tool for health and fitness enthusiasts.
  • Apple Watch SE 2: The SE 2, while still offering robust health features, is slightly pared down compared to the Series 8. It doesn’t have the ECG app or blood oxygen monitoring. However, it still provides heart rate monitoring, sleep tracking, and fall detection, along with most of the workout modes found on the Series 8. The SE 2 also features crash detection, leveraging the same accelerometer and gyroscope sensors as the Series 8.

3. Performance and Battery Life

  • Apple Watch Series 8: Both watches share the same S8 chip, ensuring fast and responsive performance. The Series 8 offers a more premium experience with its additional features and higher-quality display. In terms of battery life, both watches offer up to 18 hours of usage on a single charge, but the Series 8 includes a Low Power Mode that can extend battery life to up to 36 hours with reduced functionality.
  • Apple Watch SE 2: The SE 2, powered by the same S8 chip, delivers excellent performance at a lower price point. It matches the Series 8 in terms of battery life, also offering up to 18 hours per charge, but lacks the Low Power Mode enhancements.

4. Price

  • The Apple Series 8 is way more expensive than the SE 2 for premium used devices

5. Who Should Buy Which?

  • Apple Watch Series 8: Ideal for those who need features like the always-on display, ECG, blood oxygen monitoring, or advanced health sensors, the Series 8 is worth the investment.
  • Apple Watch SE 2: Perfect for those who want a reliable smartwatch with essential features at a more affordable price. If you don’t need the advanced health sensors or the always-on display, the SE 2 offers excellent value without compromising on performance.

Conclusion

While both the Apple Watch Series 8 and the Apple Watch SE 2 were released on the same date, they are designed for different audiences. The Series 8 is for those who want a premium smartwatch experience with the latest health and fitness features, while the SE 2 is an excellent choice for budget-conscious consumers who still want the core benefits of an Apple Watch. Your choice between them will ultimately depend on your specific needs and budget.

posts.title: 2 Stress-free Methods to Permanently Block Ads on Your Phone
posts.content:
Tired of those annoying ads popping up every time you try to enjoy your favorite app or browse the web? You're not alone! Ads can be intrusive, slow down your phone, and drain your battery. But don’t worry, Ogabassey has got you covered. Here are two stress-free methods to permanently block ads on your phone, so you can enjoy a smooth, ad-free experience.

1. Use a Dedicated Ad Blocker App

The quickest and most efficient way to block ads on your phone is by using a dedicated ad blocker app. These apps are designed specifically to keep those pesky ads at bay, whether you're browsing the internet or using apps.

How it works:

  • Step 1: Download an ad blocker app from your app store. Some popular ones include AdGuard, Blokada, and Adblock Plus.
  • Step 2: Install the app and follow the on-screen instructions to set it up. Most apps will ask for permission to create a VPN connection on your phone. This is what allows them to block ads across all your apps and browsers.
  • Step 3: Once the ad blocker is set up, it will start filtering out ads automatically. You can customize the settings to block specific types of ads or even whitelist apps where you don’t mind seeing ads.

Pros:

  • Easy to set up and use.
  • Works across all apps and browsers.
  • Customizable to your preferences.

Cons:

  • Some apps might not work correctly with an ad blocker enabled.
  • Certain ad blocker apps may require a subscription for full features.

2. Modify Your DNS Settings

Another effective method to block ads is by modifying your phone's DNS settings. This method is a bit more technical but just as effective, and it doesn’t require downloading any additional apps.

How it works:

  • Step 1: Go to your phone's settings and find the Wi-Fi or network settings section.
  • Step 2: Look for the option to change DNS settings. On most phones, this will be under the "Advanced" or "Private DNS" section.
  • Step 3: Enter the DNS address of an ad-blocking DNS server. PWe recommend using AdGuard DNS (dns.adguard.com) or NextDNS (dns.nextdns.io).
  • Step 4: Save the settings and restart your phone. Once this is done, ads will be blocked at the network level, meaning you won't see them in any apps or websites.

Pros:

  • Blocks ads at the network level.
  • No need for additional apps.
  • Works across all devices connected to the same network.

Cons:

  • Requires a bit of technical know-how.
  • Some websites might load slower or not at all if they rely heavily on ads.

Final Thoughts

Blocking ads on your phone doesn’t have to be a headache. Whether you opt for a dedicated ad blocker app or modify your DNS settings, both methods are effective and will give you a cleaner, faster, and more enjoyable mobile experience. So go ahead, try out one of these methods today, and say goodbye to annoying ads for good!

posts.title: 4 Simple Tricks to Boost Your Phone’s Performance
posts.content:
Is your phone starting to feel sluggish? Apps taking forever to load? Battery life not what it used to be? Don't worry; your phone doesn’t have to stay slow. With just a few simple tricks, you can boost your phone’s performance and make it feel almost brand new again. Let’s dive in!

1. Clear Out Unnecessary Apps and Files

One of the easiest ways to speed up your phone is by clearing out the clutter. Over time, your phone can get bogged down with apps, files, and photos that you no longer use or need. These take up valuable storage space and can slow down your device.

How to do it:

  • Step 1: Go through your apps and uninstall any that you haven’t used in the last few months.
  • Step 2: Delete old photos, videos, and files that you don’t need. You can back them up to a cloud service if you want to keep them but free up space on your device.
  • Step 3: Use a file cleaner app to remove temporary files and cache data that might be slowing down your phone.

Bonus Tip: Set a reminder to do this every few months to keep your phone running smoothly.

2. Update Your Software Regularly

Keeping your phone’s software up to date is crucial for performance. Software updates not only bring new features but also include bug fixes and performance enhancements that can make your phone run more efficiently.

How to do it:

  • Step 1: Go to your phone’s settings and check for any available software updates.
  • Step 2: Install the updates as soon as they’re available. This applies to both your operating system and the apps you have installed.

Bonus Tip: Enable automatic updates so you don’t have to worry about missing out on important improvements.

3. Limit Background Processes

Background processes can significantly slow down your phone. These are apps and services that run even when you’re not actively using them, consuming valuable memory and processing power.

How to do it:

  • Step 1: Go to your phone’s settings and find the "Battery" or "Performance" section.
  • Step 2: Look for an option to limit background activity or set apps to "sleep" when not in use.
  • Step 3: You can also manually close apps that you’re not using to free up memory.

Bonus Tip: Some phones have a built-in "Battery Saver" or "Performance Mode" that automatically optimizes background processes.

4. Restart Your Phone Regularly

It might sound too simple to be true, but restarting your phone regularly can make a big difference in performance. Restarting clears out the memory and closes any apps that are running in the background, giving your phone a fresh start.

How to do it:

  • Step 1: Simply turn off your phone and turn it back on again. Doing this once a week can help keep things running smoothly.

Bonus Tip: If your phone feels particularly sluggish, a quick restart can often fix the problem immediately.

Final Thoughts

With these four simple tricks, you can easily boost your phone’s performance and keep it running like new. Regular maintenance, from clearing out clutter to updating software and limiting background processes, can make a world of difference. So go ahead, give your phone the care it deserves, and enjoy a faster, smoother experience!

posts.title: 6 Phone Habits That Deteriorate Your Battery
posts.content:
Ah, the dreaded low battery alert—the ultimate reminder that our beloved smartphones aren't invincible. If your phone's battery drains faster than your patience waiting for it to charge, chances are you're guilty of some habits that are quietly killing your battery. Don't worry; we’ve all been there! Here are 6 phone habits that are probably deteriorating your battery, and some easy fixes that’ll help you avoid the constant scramble for a charger. We have identified some these issues HERE in the past

1. Charging Your Phone Overnight

It’s so easy, right? You plug your phone in before bed and wake up with a fully charged device. But charging overnight isn’t as harmless as it seems. Overcharging can heat up your battery, and that’s a surefire way to wear it down faster than you can say "Good morning."

What to do instead:
Unplug your phone once it’s charged to around 80-90%. If you must charge overnight, use a smart plug or charging pad that automatically stops when your phone reaches full charge.

2. Draining Your Battery to 0% Every Time

Do you wait until your phone is gasping for life at 1% before plugging it in? Draining your battery to 0% regularly is like running your car until the gas tank is bone dry—it’s just not a good idea.

What to do instead:
Try to keep your phone’s charge between 20% and 80%. That’s the sweet spot for most batteries. Your phone will thank you later.

3. Using Your Phone While It’s Charging

We’ve all been guilty of this one—scrolling through Instagram or watching YouTube while the phone is plugged in. But using your phone while it’s charging generates extra heat, and heat is basically kryptonite to your battery.

What to do instead:
Put your phone down and let it charge in peace. It’ll charge faster and stay cooler, which means a happier, healthier battery.

4. Cranking Up the Brightness

Sure, a bright screen looks great, but it’s also one of the biggest battery killers. Every time you turn your brightness up to max, you’re telling your battery to work overtime.

What to do instead:
Use auto-brightness or dim your screen manually when you’re indoors. And let’s be real, do you really need your screen to light up like a lighthouse at all times?

5. Never Turning Off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi

If your Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are always on, even when you're not using them, you're basically inviting your battery to drain itself. These features constantly search for devices and networks, consuming power even when idle.

What to do instead:
Turn off Bluetooth and Wi-Fi when you’re not using them, especially when you’re out and about. Bonus: You’ll also stop your phone from awkwardly trying to connect to random networks.

6. Letting Notifications Run Wild

Between emails, social media, and app alerts, it feels like our phones never stop buzzing. But each notification lights up your screen and wakes up your phone’s battery for no reason. Every little buzz chips away at your battery life.

What to do instead:
Silence non-essential notifications. Do you really need to know about every single “like” on Instagram right away? Keep the alerts that matter and mute the rest.

Final Thoughts

It’s easy to develop some bad phone habits without even realizing it. But by making a few small adjustments, you can keep your battery healthier for longer—and avoid those frantic “where’s my charger?” moments. So, give your phone a break, stop treating it like a power-hungry drama queen, and let it live its best, longest-lasting life!

posts.title: How to Choose the Perfect Laptop for Your Needs in 2024
posts.content:
Whether you’re upgrading from an old machine or buying your very first laptop, 2024 brings some exciting new trends in laptop technology. With so many options available, finding the right laptop can be a challenge. But don’t worry—Ogabassey has got you covered! Here’s our comprehensive guide to help you choose the perfect laptop for your needs.

1. Minimum RAM: 8GB or More

Let’s start with the basics: RAM. In 2024, 8GB of RAM should be your absolute minimum for any laptop. Anything less and you’ll likely face performance issues with multiple open tabs, applications, or background processes. However, if you're into gaming, video editing, or running software like Adobe Photoshop, consider going for 16GB or 32GB for a smoother experience.

2. Platform: Windows, macOS, or ChromeOS?

Your laptop's operating system (OS) is key to productivity:

  • Windows: Offers a wide range of options and supports most software, making it ideal for business, gaming, and general use.
  • macOS: Best for creative professionals who use apps like Final Cut Pro or Logic Pro. Apple's ecosystem and M1/M2/M3 chips also provide great performance. Gaming is not macOS’s strongest suit, so, if you would like to game on your laptop, Windows is probably your best option. Conversely, apps optimisation is on another level on macOS and if you an iPhone user, the interconnectivity between your iPhone and your MacBook is another compelling reason to go Apple again, after all, once you go Apple, you don’t go back!
  • ChromeOS: Perfect for light tasks, students, or budget users. It's a cloud-based OS but can handle web browsing, streaming, and basic productivity well. The major downsize to the ChromeOS is that it requires internet connection to really work well.

Choose the platform that aligns with your daily tasks and software requirements.

3. Processor: The Brain of Your Laptop

In 2024, the Intel 13th Gen and AMD Ryzen 7000 series are ruling the market, with Apple’s M1/M2/M3 chips excelling on macOS devices.

  • For basic tasks (browsing, streaming, and word processing): Intel Core i5 or AMD Ryzen 5 will serve you well.
  • For high performance (content creation, gaming, programming): Opt for Intel Core i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 7/9.

The right processor will ensure that your laptop handles tasks efficiently without slowing down.

4. Storage: SSD is a Must

Say goodbye to traditional hard drives. In 2024, SSD (Solid State Drive) is non-negotiable for speed and reliability. At a minimum, go for 256GB SSD, but if you deal with large files (like high-resolution videos or games), consider 512GB or more.

5. Biometrics for Added Security

Laptops today come with advanced security options. Biometric authentication is increasingly common, including:

  • Fingerprint scanners: Quick and secure login.
  • Facial recognition: Available on some high-end models for seamless and secure access.

These features enhance security and make logging in faster and more convenient.

6. Display & Screen Resolution: Clarity Matters

Your laptop's display is important, especially if you spend hours working or streaming content. Please avoid HD screens if you can, the resolution is outdated and will be useless for any graphics-related task. The recommended standard today is:

  • Full HD (1920x1080): Great for most tasks, from watching movies to handling office work.
  • 4K resolution: Ideal for professionals in video editing or graphic design who need ultra-clear visuals.

Also, consider screen size—13-inch to 15-inch models are generally the sweet spot for portability and usability. However, if you’re gaming or editing videos, a 17-inch screen may be more suitable.

7. Battery Life: Don’t Be Tethered

Nothing’s worse than your laptop dying in the middle of a presentation or binge-watching session. Aim for a laptop with at least 8-10 hours of battery life. Battery life depends on factors like screen brightness and usage, so check reviews for real-world performance. Apple M-series laptops have set the standard for efficiency with the M1 MacBook Air averaging an insane 18 hours of usage. Newer Intel and AMD laptops also have similar levels of battery performance.

8. Ports: Connectivity Options Matter

Having the right ports can make all the difference, especially if you use accessories like external monitors, hard drives, or headsets. Common ports in 2024 include:

  • USB-C: The new standard for charging and data transfer.
  • Thunderbolt 4 (usually over USB-C): Ideal for fast data transfer and connecting external GPUs.
  • HDMI: Handy for connecting to larger displays or projectors.
  • 3.5mm headphone jack: Don’t overlook this if you prefer wired audio.

Be sure the laptop has the right combination of ports to match your needs.

9. Graphics Card: Integrated vs Dedicated

For light tasks, an integrated graphics card (Intel Iris Xe, AMD Radeon) will do just fine. However, if you’re into gaming or heavy graphical work (3D rendering, video editing), go for a laptop with a dedicated GPU like NVIDIA RTX 30 series or AMD Radeon RX.

10. Budget: Spend Wisely

While it’s tempting to go for the latest and greatest, pick a laptop within your budget that meets your needs. In 2024, a solid all-purpose laptop with 8GB RAM, an Intel Core i5 processor (8th-11th gen intel and AMD equivalents), and a Full HD display will cost around ₦500,000 - ₦800,000. For high-performance laptops, expect to pay upwards of ₦1.2 million.

If you’re looking to save some money, don’t overlook the used or refurbished laptop market. Ogabassey offers UK used laptops at affordable prices with the option to pay in instalments. Send us a DM on Instagram to get started.  

Choosing the perfect laptop in 2024 is all about balancing performance, features, and budget. Identify your primary needs, then match them with the right specs and features, and you’ll land a laptop that will serve you well for years to come. Tell us your use case in the comments section and we will recommend an affordable laptop that suits your need.

Happy laptop shopping!

If you’re a creative professional or someone who works with resource-intensive applications, the Pro’s superior performance will make a noticeable difference.

2. Portability: Ultra-Light or Slightly Heavier

  • MacBook Air: One of the MacBook Air’s strongest selling points is its lightweight and slim design. Weighing under three pounds, it’s incredibly easy to carry around. Whether you're constantly commuting, working from coffee shops, or traveling, the MacBook Air is the perfect companion for those who prioritize portability.
  • MacBook Pro: While still quite portable, the MacBook Pro is a bit heavier due to its more robust design and additional features. The 13-inch model is still easy to lug around, but if you opt for the larger 14- or 16-inch versions, you’ll feel the added weight in your bag. That said, the extra heft is a trade-off for the enhanced performance and features.

3. Battery Life: All-Day Power

  • MacBook Air: The MacBook Air is known for delivering outstanding battery life, making it ideal for long workdays without needing to reach for a charger. Whether you're taking notes in class, working remotely, or watching movies during a Netflix and Chill session on your bed, you can count on the Air to last through the day.
  • MacBook Pro: The MacBook Pro also offers impressive battery life, but it can vary depending on how intensively you’re using the machine. For standard use like web browsing and document editing, it performs similarly to the Air. However, if you’re running heavier programs or working with graphics, the battery might drain faster. Still, you can expect it to last through most of your workday without needing to recharge.

4. Price: Budget-Friendly vs. Premium Power

  • MacBook Air: The MacBook Air is generally the more affordable option, offering great value for users who don’t need high-end specs. If you're someone who needs a dependable laptop for general use without breaking the bank, the Air is an excellent investment. It’s perfect for students, casual users, and professionals who primarily use office applications and web-based tools.
  • MacBook Pro: The MacBook Pro comes with a higher price tag, but it’s well worth it for users who require more power and advanced features. If you need a laptop that can handle heavy-duty tasks like video editing, 3D rendering, or running professional-grade software, the extra cost of the Pro is justified. It’s designed for professionals and creatives who need top-tier performance in their day-to-day work.

5. Display & Graphics: Good Enough or Exceptional?

  • MacBook Air: With its vibrant Retina display, the MacBook Air provides crisp visuals, sharp text, and a high-quality viewing experience that is more than sufficient for most users. Whether you’re watching Netflix, editing photos, or working on presentations, the Air’s screen delivers excellent clarity and colour.
  • MacBook Pro: The MacBook Pro takes things up a notch with an even better display. Larger screen options and enhanced colour accuracy make it the go-to choice for professionals who work with graphics, video, or design. If a superior display and more advanced graphics performance are crucial to your workflow, the Pro’s high-quality screen is a major plus.

Which One Should You Choose?

  • MacBook Air: Choose the Air if you’re looking for a light, portable laptop that can handle everyday tasks with ease. It’s ideal for students, professionals with basic computing needs, and casual users who want a reliable machine at a lower price point.
  • MacBook Pro: Opt for the MacBook Pro if you need a high-performance laptop that can handle demanding tasks like video editing, graphic design, or intensive multitasking. If you’re a professional who works with resource-heavy applications or simply need a laptop that can do it all, the Pro’s extra power is worth the investment.

In 2024, the choice between the MacBook Air and MacBook Pro comes down to how much performance you need versus how much portability you prefer. Both are excellent options, but knowing your specific needs will help guide your decision. Whether you’re a student, a creative professional, or a business user, Apple’s MacBook lineup has the perfect device for you. Which one will you pick?

posts.title: From Amateur to Grandmaster: 6 Game-Changing SKills to Master iPhone Photography
posts.content:
In today's world, the iPhone has become more than just a tool for communication; it’s also a powerful camera in your pocket. Whether you're capturing moments with friends or trying to step up your Instagram game, mastering iPhone photography can help your pictures stand out. If you’ve ever wondered how to take your shots from basic to brilliant, these six tips will have you snapping like a pro in no time!

1. Master the Basics of Composition

Composition is everything when it comes to creating visually appealing photos. Here are two techniques you should definitely explore:

  • Rule of Thirds: One simple but effective way to improve your photo composition is to enable the grid feature in your camera settings. Place your subject along the grid lines or at their intersections to create a more balanced and engaging shot.
  • Leading Lines: Use natural lines—like roads, pathways, or buildings—to guide the viewer’s eyes directly to your main subject. This technique draws attention where it matters most.

2. Utilise Lighting Effectively

Lighting can make or break a photo, and the iPhone’s advanced features help you get it just right:

  • Golden Hour: Photographers rave about the golden hour for good reason. This magical time—right after sunrise or just before sunset—offers soft, warm lighting that flatters any subject.
  • Night Mode: For those evening or dimly lit moments, iPhone’s Night Mode is a game-changer. It captures impressive detail and reduces noise, ensuring your low-light photos come out sharp and clear.

3. Explore Camera Settings

Your iPhone is packed with settings that let you take full control of your photography experience:

  • ProRAW: If you’re using an iPhone 12 Pro or newer, switch to ProRAW format for more control during editing. This format retains more detail and gives you the flexibility to fine-tune your photos later.
  • Portrait Mode: If you're looking to create stunning portraits, this mode gives you a shallow depth of field, allowing your subject to stand out against a beautifully blurred background.

4. Experiment with Angles and Perspectives

Stop shooting from eye level! Switch things up with different angles:

  • Low and High Angles: Try taking photos from a low or high perspective to make your shots more dynamic. You'll be surprised how much difference a fresh angle can make.
  • Macro Mode: For those intricate close-ups, newer iPhone models offer a Macro Mode that lets you capture stunning details—whether it’s a raindrop or the fine texture of a leaf.

5. Edit Your Photos

A little post-production can turn a good photo into a great one:

  • Editing Apps: Apps like Adobe Lightroom or Snapseed can take your images to the next level. Adjust things like exposure, contrast, and colour balance to really make your photos pop.
  • Non-Destructive Editing: Always aim for non-destructive editing by using layers and masks. This way, you can experiment with different adjustments without permanently altering the original image.

6. Stay Inspired and Keep Learning

The best photographers never stop learning:

  • Photography Blogs and Tutorials: Keep up with the latest trends and tips by following photography blogs or watching online tutorials. There’s always something new to learn!

Final Thoughts

By incorporating these six tips into your iPhone photography routine, you'll quickly see an improvement in the quality of your shots. Whether it's mastering composition or learning how to use lighting to your advantage, every step you take will bring you closer to grandmaster-level photography. So, get out there, start shooting, and let your creativity flow. Happy snapping!

posts.title: Apple Intelligence: What You Need to Know About Apple\'s Latest AI Innovation

What is Apple Intelligence?

Apple Intelligence is a collection of AI-driven features that aim to make your user experience smoother and more efficient. By using machine learning and large language models directly on your device, it can do things like:

Samsung’s cloud storage keeps your photos, videos, and files synced across all your devices. Never worry about losing data when switching between your phone and laptop; Samsung Cloud has it all backed up and ready.

Samsung’s ecosystem isn’t just about owning multiple devices; it’s about creating a seamless, interconnected experience that makes life easier. By integrating your Galaxy devices, you’ll unlock new levels of productivity, entertainment, and smart living.

posts.title: Maximize Your iPhone: Pro Tips for Creating Killer Content on Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok
posts.content:
Are you considering becoming a content creator or you’re looking to level up your content game without investing in expensive cameras? There is something you have been sleeping on and we are here to share the tea with you. What if we tell you that your iPhone can be your all-in-one production tool. Whether you're posting on Instagram, YouTube, or TikTok, mastering your iPhone’s capabilities can help you create stunning visuals that stand out in a crowded feed.

Here’s how to transform your iPhone into a pro-level camera for your social media content.

1. Know Your iPhone Camera Settings

Your iPhone comes loaded with powerful camera settings that can take your content from basic to professional. Here’s what you should focus on:

  • Resolution & Frame Rate: Go into your settings and choose 4K resolution for crisp, detailed videos. A frame rate of 30fps works well for social media, but if you’re aiming for that smooth cinematic effect, or you wish to add some slow-mo to portions of your video during postproduction, you can switch to 60fps.
  • HDR Mode: Make sure to enable High Dynamic Range (HDR) to capture more detail in both highlights and shadows, which makes your visuals pop.
  • Grid Lines: Turn on grid lines to use the "rule of thirds" for balanced, aesthetically pleasing shots.

2. Stabilize Your Shots

Shaky footage can ruin an otherwise perfect video. Use a tripod or gimbal to keep your shots steady. If you're filming on the go, activate your iPhone’s Cinematic Mode or use the in-built Optical Image Stabilization (available on newer models like the iPhone 13 Pro and above) to smooth out movement.

3. Use the Right Lighting

Lighting is everything in photography and videography. If you’re filming indoors, make use of softbox lights or ring lights for a flattering glow. When outdoors, shoot during the "golden hour" (just after sunrise or before sunset) to capture warm, natural light that looks stunning on screen.

For quick fixes, the iPhone's built-in flash works in a pinch, but a portable LED light might be a more reliable option for consistent quality.

4. Enhance Your Audio Quality

Great visuals need great sound. While the iPhone’s microphone is decent, using an external mic, like a lapel or shotgun mic, can drastically improve audio clarity. You’ll notice a huge difference in engagement when your sound is crisp, especially on YouTube and TikTok.

5. Editing on Your iPhone

You don’t need fancy software to edit your videos. Your iPhone offers editing tools right in the Photos app, but if you want to step up your game:

  • iMovie: This app is perfect for quick edits, transitions, and adding music.
  • LumaFusion: A more advanced app for professional-level video editing, perfect for YouTube creators.
  • Capcut: Ideal for social media edits, offering features like text, stickers, and music overlays for Instagram Reels and TikToks.

6. Leverage Slow-Mo and Time-Lapse

Create dynamic content by experimenting with slow-motion and time-lapse modes. Slow-mo videos, especially in 240fps, add dramatic flair, while time-lapse can capture longer processes in seconds—perfect for behind-the-scenes or "day in the life" videos.

7. Use Lenses and Accessories

For more versatility, try clip-on lenses like wide-angle, macro, or fish-eye lenses. They’re affordable and can give your videos and photos a creative edge. You can also invest in accessories like a lens cleaning kit to keep your camera spotless.

8. Shoot Vertical and Horizontal

For Instagram Stories and TikToks, vertical shooting is a must. But when you're filming for YouTube, always shoot horizontally. Make sure to switch between these orientations depending on your platform to avoid awkward cropping during post-production.

Final Thoughts

Your iPhone is an incredibly powerful tool that can create high-quality content for Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok without the need for expensive gear. By mastering your camera settings, using proper lighting, and editing efficiently, you can produce content that looks professional and keeps your audience coming back for more.

Ready to take your content to the next level? Grab your iPhone and start shooting!

Let’s explore how you can fully harness this ecosystem to supercharge your productivity and creativity.

The Joy of Being in the Apple Ecosystem

Imagine starting an email on your iPhone while you’re on the move, only to seamlessly pick up exactly where you left off on your MacBook when you sit down at your desk. Or, better yet, receiving a phone call on your iPhone while it’s charging across the room and answering it directly on your MacBook. This kind of cohesion is what makes the Apple ecosystem so powerful.

Apple’s ecosystem is designed for convenience and fluidity. Features like Continuity, Handoff, and iCloud ensure that your work, media, and even your personal preferences are synced between devices. It feels almost magical when your clipboard syncs across your devices or when you copy text from your iPhone and paste it directly into your MacBook. It’s these little things that make the experience so rewarding, especially for multitaskers, content creators, and business professionals alike.

Essential Tips to Maximize the iPhone-MacBook Duo

1. Use Handoff for Seamless Transitions

With Handoff, you can start tasks on one device and continue them on another. For instance, if you’re writing a document on Pages or browsing on Safari, you can effortlessly pick it up on your MacBook without having to send it or save it somewhere first. Just look for the app icon in the Dock on your Mac or in the App Switcher on your iPhone.

2. iCloud Drive: Keep Everything in Sync

If you’re not using iCloud Drive, you’re missing out. By syncing your files across devices, you can access your documents, photos, and notes from anywhere, anytime. Turn it on, and you’ll never have to worry about whether you saved that presentation on your iPhone or Mac—it’ll be available on both.

3. Instant Hotspot: Stay Connected on the Go

Forgot to connect to Wi-Fi or don’t have access to one? No problem! Your MacBook can use your iPhone’s cellular data connection via Instant Hotspot, without needing to grab your phone. Just click the Wi-Fi icon on your MacBook, and your iPhone will appear as a hotspot option.

4. AirDrop for Quick File Transfers

Need to quickly share a file, photo, or document between devices? AirDrop is your best friend. It allows you to send and receive files instantly between your iPhone and MacBook with just a few taps or clicks, and it’s far faster than traditional methods like emailing yourself a file.

5. Universal Clipboard: Copy and Paste Across Devices

Universal Clipboard is a game-changer for those who constantly shift between their iPhone and MacBook. You can copy text, images, or even entire files on one device and paste them onto another. For example, copy a phone number from a website on your MacBook and paste it directly into your iPhone’s contacts app.

6. Sidecar: Turn Your iPhone into an Extra Display

If you’re working on a MacBook but want some extra screen space, you can turn your iPhone into a second display using Sidecar. It’s a handy feature for graphic designers, video editors, or anyone who enjoys multitasking. Just connect your devices wirelessly, and you can drag windows from your MacBook to your iPhone’s screen for more room.

7. Answer Calls and Texts on Your MacBook

You don’t need to reach for your iPhone every time you receive a call or text. Thanks to Continuity, you can handle these directly from your MacBook. Whether it's a FaceTime call, a regular phone call, or even text messages, everything shows up on your computer screen, keeping you focused and efficient.

Conclusion

When your iPhone and MacBook work together, they create a seamless digital ecosystem that saves time, boosts productivity, and simply makes life easier. Apple has designed these devices to complement each other perfectly, so if you’re lucky enough to own both, make sure you’re taking full advantage of all the integrated features. Whether you’re a student, a professional, or just someone who loves efficiency, getting the best out of this duo will change the way you work and play.

Are you using your iPhone and MacBook to their full potential yet? Let us know which features you’re loving the most!

posts.title: Unleash Your Samsung Camera: Top Tips for Creating Stunning Content on Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok
posts.content:
One of the myths about creating content on a budget that has refused to die is that you need an iPhone to do shoot appealing videos. Nothing could be farther from the truth, in the hand of a master, most smartphones cameras are more than can capable of outputing serviceable clips. Yes, the iPhone is an incredible device, we have explained here how you can turn your iPhone into a content creation beast, but it’s not the only phone capable of the magical.   With the advanced features packed into Samsung phones, you’ve got everything you need right in your hand to create amazing videos. Let’s dive into how you can turn your Samsung into a powerhouse for pro-level content creation.

1. Optimize Samsung’s Camera Modes for Your Content

Samsung phones, particularly flagships like the Galaxy S series, are known for their incredible camera systems. Here’s how to get the most out of them:

  • Resolution & Frame Rate: Dial up the quality by shooting in 8K if your phone supports it, or stick with 4K for clearer visuals and manageable file sizes. For buttery smooth videos, set the frame rate to 60fps, especially for action shots or TikToks that involve movement.
  • Pro Video Mode: Want total control? Switch to Pro Video Mode and tweak settings like ISO, focus, and exposure to nail that perfect shot—something many creators love about Samsung.
  • Single Take: This unique feature lets you capture multiple types of media—photos, videos, and clips—all at once. Ideal for creating variety when you’re not sure what format works best.

2. Get Rid of the Shakes with Built-In Stabilization

Samsung excels at video stabilization with its Super Steady Mode. Whether you're filming a dynamic vlog for YouTube or shooting on the move for TikTok, this feature ensures you get smooth footage, even without a tripod. If you’re using one of the newer Galaxy models, combine this with the phone’s Optical Image Stabilization (OIS) for professional results.

3. Edit Like a Pro with Samsung’s Tools

Editing can be a breeze if you use Samsung’s built-in tools. Samsung Gallery offers basic video trimming and color correction, but if you’re looking for a more polished result, try these apps:

  • Adobe Premiere Rush: Perfect for creating high-quality, professional videos on the go.
  • YouCut: A free, user-friendly video editor ideal for social media clips, offering transitions, text overlays, and background music.
  • Samsung’s Expert RAW: If you’re into heavy post-processing, shoot in RAW format to give you more room to play with your visuals during editing.

4. Take Advantage of Hyperlapse and Super Slow-mo

Samsung phones give you more than just regular video options. Hyperlapse is great for speeding up long events or capturing cityscapes over time. For the opposite effect, Super Slow-mo (up to 960fps) will let you capture jaw-dropping details that are otherwise too fast for the naked eye—perfect for TikTok effects or dramatic reveals.

5. Enhance Your Creativity with Extra Lenses

Samsung’s multi-lens setup—which often includes ultra-wide, telephoto, and macro lenses—gives you versatility in your shots. Use the ultra-wide lens to capture sweeping landscapes or large group shots, and the macro lens for up-close, detailed photography. For even more creative control, try attaching third-party lenses for fisheye or anamorphic effects.

6. Match the Format to the Platform

Samsung makes it easy to switch between shooting modes. For TikTok and Instagram Stories, shoot vertically, but when creating for YouTube, always film horizontally for a more professional look. If you’re repurposing content across platforms, batch shoot and then reframe the content to fit each platform’s preferred format.

7. Maximize the Power of AI

Samsung’s AI features, like the Galaxy AI,  Scene Optimizer and Auto Framing, can intelligently adjust settings based on the environment. Scene Optimizer recognizes up to 30 different subjects and automatically tweaks your settings for the best shot. Meanwhile, Auto Framing tracks your movement to keep you in the center of the shot—perfect for solo YouTube creators or dance videos on TikTok.

Final Thoughts

Your Samsung phone is packed with powerful features designed to help you create amazing content for Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. With the right techniques and a bit of creativity, you can turn your phone into a full-fledged content creation machine. Ready to hit record? Take your Samsung out of your pocket, and let your content shine!

posts.title: Everything You Need to Know About the Apple M4 Chip
posts.content:
As big fans of Apple's M series, we have written extensively about them here and here, we are giddy with joy with the promise of the M4. Apple first teased the power of the M4 chip with its release in the iPad Pro earlier this year, sparking excitement but also some frustration—many agree the M4's true potential can’t be fully utilized on the iPad due to iPadOS constraints. Now, Apple has revealed the full capabilities of the M4 lineup with new MacBook, iMac, and Mac Mini models. And if the performance stats are anything to go by, this could very well be the most powerful chip in any consumer-grade PC, especially for AI-focused tasks. Move over Snapdragon Elite Processor, Intel Core Ultra 200, and AMD Ryzen 9 HX 370!

The M4 series includes four versions: the standard M4 (with 8 or 10 CPU cores), the M4 Pro (with up to 20 GPU cores), and the M4 Max. Each model delivers substantial boosts in graphics performance, with up to 2x faster ray tracing and a dramatically enhanced Neural Engine (or NPU, familiar to those in the PC Copilot+ crowd). In the Mac lineup, we’re also seeing impressive new features like multiple-display support on the standard M4 and Thunderbolt 5 on the M4 Pro, which cranks up data transfer speeds to new heights. Add to that the 273GB/s memory bandwidth—double that of any PC AI chip—this processor is a multitasking powerhouse. For a lot of people, the most exciting information about the M4 powered MacBook is Apple's claim that the battery will last for 24 hours. That is wild!

Who Is the M4 Chip For?

The M4 chip isn't just another processor upgrade—it’s designed for those who demand serious power and efficiency, particularly users pushing the boundaries in AI, video editing, 3D rendering, and high-performance gaming. Here’s a closer look at the people who’ll benefit the most from Apple’s latest powerhouse:

  1. AI Enthusiasts and Developers: The M4’s Neural Engine is a game-changer, allowing machine learning and AI workloads to run with blazing efficiency. For those experimenting with AI models or using machine learning for app development, the M4’s boosted NPU and 2x faster ray tracing can handle complex calculations faster and more accurately.
  2. Creative Professionals: Designers, video editors, and animators will feel the difference in the M4 Pro and M4 Max versions, which offer enhanced GPU performance and support for multiple displays. Whether you’re editing high-resolution video or working with large graphics files, these chips reduce rendering times and streamline workflows with their high memory bandwidth and upgraded graphics.
  3. Engineers and Scientists: For users in fields that require powerful simulations or data-heavy computations, like software engineering, biotechnology, or physics, the M4 Pro’s Thunderbolt 5 compatibility and the M4 Max’s memory bandwidth can dramatically improve multitasking and data transfer speeds.
  4. Everyday Multitaskers: If you’re the kind of user who always has dozens of tabs, applications, and projects open simultaneously, the M4’s increased RAM support and memory bandwidth make it a multitasking powerhouse. Even on the standard M4, users will find switching between tasks smoother and more responsive than ever.
  5. Mac Loyalists Looking to Future-Proof: For anyone who relies on Apple’s ecosystem and wants a Mac that will stay competitive for years to come, the M4’s architecture and compatibility with macOS Sequoia’s Apple Intelligence make it a solid investment.

Apple’s AI assistant, Apple Intelligence, debuts with macOS Sequoia on the M4 Macs, though a fully polished version is expected by December. And yes, Apple has reserved this feature exclusively for its M-series MacBooks, leaving Intel-based Macs out in the cold.

For the first time, all base models (MacBook Pro, Mac Mini, and iMac) now come with 16GB of RAM as standard. However, true to Apple’s tradition, they still cap the base storage at 256GB. If you need more storage, expect to pay a premium—unfortunately, the SSDs are non-upgradable.

Here in the office, we can’t wait to get our hands on these new machines. If you’re looking to get a MacBook Air with the M4, though, you’ll need to wait until next year.

So, are you planning to snag the new M4 MacBook Pro? Let us know what you think!

posts.title: Choosing the Right iPad: Pro, Air, or Mini?
posts.content:
Tablets have become the ultimate hybrid between phones and laptops, offering the portability of a smartphone with the power and versatility of a computer. And when it comes to tablets, Apple's iPad line has long set the standard. Despite the recent rise of foldable phones that combine the functionality of a phone with a larger screen, iPads continue to lead the pack in popularity and capability. With a range of models from the powerful iPad Pro to the portable iPad Mini, Apple’s tablets remain the go-to choice for users who want that perfect middle ground—a device that’s bigger than a phone, more portable than a laptop, and loaded with features to support work, creativity, and entertainment. Each model brings unique features to the table, whether you’re looking for professional-grade performance, a balanced all-rounder, or a compact device to slip into your bag. So, which one is right for you? We have focused on the latest generation for each category. In our subsequent posts we will spotlight the older generations.

 Let’s dive into what sets the iPad Pro, iPad Air, and iPad Mini apart to find the perfect fit.

1. iPad Pro: The Powerhouse

If you're after the ultimate performance and can splurge a bit, the iPad Pro is a no-brainer. It comes in 13-inch Tandem OLED Ultra Retina XDR with ProMotion, or 11-inch Tandem OLED Ultra Retina XDR with ProMotion, equipped with either the Apple’s M4 chip (13-inch) or M2 chip , the same powerhouse chip used in Macs. This makes it lightning-fast, perfect for multitasking, graphic-intensive tasks, and high-performance apps like Photoshop or 4K video editing.

Highlights of the iPad Pro:

  • Display: With a Tandem OLED Ultra Retina XDR with ProMotion (13-inch model) or Tandem OLED Ultra Retina XDR with ProMotion (especially in the 11-inch model), you get breathtaking colours and crisp clarity. Great for content creators, photographers, and anyone who values top-notch visuals.
  • Performance: The M4 or the M2 chip ensure speed and efficiency, enabling smooth multitasking and support for advanced apps.
  • Features: Supports the latest Apple Pencil and Magic Keyboard, transforming it into a versatile workstation. Plus, the Pro’s Face ID unlock is a treat for seamless security.

Who’s it for? This model is ideal for professionals and creatives who need top-tier performance, whether it’s for design, video editing, or note-taking in the most fluid way possible.

2. iPad Air: The Best of Both Worlds

The iPad Air is like the sweet spot between affordability and power. It’s less expensive than the iPad Pro but still packs a punch, especially with the M1 chip onboard, which handles pretty much everything a casual user could throw at it.

Highlights of the iPad Air:

  • Display: It’s got a 10.9-inch Liquid Retina display, bright and clear with True Tone technology.
  • Performance: Thanks to the M2 chip, the Air holds up well even with demanding apps, from casual gaming to productivity tools.
  • Features: Supports the second-generation Apple Pencil and Magic Keyboard, making it a strong choice for students and casual creators. It uses Touch ID on the power button instead of Face ID, which is convenient and secure.

Who’s it for?
The iPad Air is great for students, professionals, or anyone who wants a capable tablet without going all-in on the Pro. It can handle multitasking and creativity apps with ease but won’t break the bank.

3. iPad Mini: The Pocket-Friendly Option

The iPad Mini is in a league of its own. It’s ultra-portable, with an 8.3-inch display that’s easy to hold in one hand, making it perfect for on-the-go users who need a compact yet capable device.

Highlights of the iPad Mini:

  • Display: Although smaller, it’s still a Liquid Retina display with True Tone and P3 wide colour for vibrant visuals.
  • Performance: The A15 Bionic chip (same as the iPhone 13) powers the Mini, giving it strong performance in a compact form.
  • Features: Supports the second-gen Apple Pencil, so you can still sketch, annotate, or take notes comfortably. It uses Touch ID like the Air.

Who’s it for? If you’re always on the go or prefer a compact device for reading, quick notes, or light productivity, the iPad Mini is your best bet. It’s especially useful for people who don’t need a big screen but still want the iPad experience.

Comparison at a Glance

Which One Should You Go For?

  • Go for the iPad Pro if you need top-tier performance for creative or professional work. It’s worth the investment if you plan to use it as a laptop replacement or if you’re big on visual content creation.
  • Opt for the iPad Air if you want great performance without the premium Pro price tag. It’s balanced enough to handle most tasks while being budget friendly.
  • Choose the iPad Mini if portability is your priority. It’s a perfect on-the-go device, offering just enough power for daily tasks and light creativity without weighing you down.

Final Thoughts

Your choice really comes down to how you plan to use your iPad. The Pro is a top-tier powerhouse, the Air is a fantastic all-rounder, and the Mini is unbeatable for portability. Each has its strengths, so think about what you’ll be using it for, and let that guide your decision. Happy shopping!

posts.title: PS5 Pro: To Upgrade or Not to is the Question
posts.content:
In the gaming world, few brands command as much loyalty as Sony’s PlayStation. Despite Microsoft’s determined efforts with Xbox, PlayStation continues to dominate the console market. So, when Sony introduces a new version, the industry listens. The latest release, the PlayStation 5 Pro, launched last week to a mixed reception from the gaming community, largely due to its $700 price tag. Is the PS5 Pro worth the investment? Here’s a breakdown of what the PS5 Pro offers and whether it justifies an upgrade.

Key Upgrades: What’s New?

The PS5 Pro boasts three primary enhancements: a more powerful GPU, advanced ray-tracing capabilities, and Sony's new AI-based upscaling technology called PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), comparable to Nvidia’s DLSS. Here’s what those upgrades translate to in real-world gameplay:

  • Improved Graphics Performance: The GPU in the PS5 Pro is touted to deliver 45% more power, alongside 28% faster memory for quicker in-game rendering.
  • Ray Tracing: Enhanced raytracing brings realistic lighting and reflections, making scenes feel more immersive.
  • 2TB SSD: Double the storage compared to the standard PS5, allowing for a bigger game library without needing immediate external storage.

However, the PS5 Pro omits a few staples of previous generations—there’s no built-in disc drive, and the vertical stand is sold separately.

Design and Build: Familiar Yet Refined

The PS5 Pro maintains the iconic design of the original PS5 but incorporates subtle refinements. Black stripes give it a sleeker look, and the unit is slightly longer than the original PS5, offering improved cooling efficiency. While there’s no disc version, it supports USB slots for external storage and has a faster Wi-Fi 7 capability, ensuring smoother online gameplay and streaming.

Storage Capacity and Expandability

One of the strongest appeals of the PS5 Pro is its expanded 2TB storage. Gamers can install a larger array of games without worrying about space. Additionally, Sony includes an M.2 SSD slot, allowing users to add even more storage if needed, making it easy to use existing SSDs from the original PS5.

Is the Price Worth It?

At $700 (almost 1.3 million Naira) MSRP, the PlayStation 5 Pro offers no discernible value proposition-make no mistake, this is an expensive console. For hardcore gamers who crave top-tier performance, enhanced visuals, and smoother gameplay, the PS5 Pro offers barely enough improvements to justify the cost. On the other hand, gamers satisfied with the original PS5 may find no justification for the price, especially since many titles continue to run well on the base model.

Final Verdict: Upgrade or Stay Put?

If you’re an enthusiast looking for the latest and greatest, the PS5 Pro delivers advanced capabilities that could enhance your gaming experience. But for casual gamers, the original PS5 likely still offers excellent value and performance. Ultimately, the decision boils down to how much the added graphics and processing power matter to your gaming style.

posts.title: Pro vs. Pro Max: Which iPhone is Right for You?
posts.content:
Every Year, iPhone users are faced with a critical question: Which iPhone should I get this year? For many, the debate boils down to the Pro and the Pro Max models. Both offer stellar performance, cutting-edge features, and that unmistakable Apple polish. But which one truly suits your needs? Here’s a guide to help you navigate the decision-making process.

1. Size Matters: Do You Prefer Compact or Bold?

The first and most obvious difference is size.

  • Pro: Slightly smaller with a more pocket-friendly design, ideal for one-handed use. If you’re someone who values portability, this might be your best bet.
  • Pro Max: A larger display that’s perfect for content consumption, multitasking, or simply enjoying those vibrant HDR videos in all their glory. However, it’s not as comfortable to hold for extended periods.

2. Battery Life: Are You Always on the Go?

With a larger body comes a bigger battery. The Pro Max consistently outlasts its smaller sibling in battery tests. If you’re someone who’s always on the move and hates carrying a charger, the Pro Max will give you that extra juice to get through your day.

However, the Pro is no slouch either—it’s more than capable of handling a full day of moderate use.

3. Camera Capabilities: Are You a Casual Photographer or a Content Creator?

The Pro Max often boasts slight enhancements in its camera system compared to the Pro, such as improved zoom capabilities or advanced stabilization (as found in the iPhone 15 Pro and the 15 Pro Max). While the differences are usually minor, they matter if you’re a content creator or professional photographer looking for the best tools for your craft.

For everyday users, though, the Pro’s camera system is more than enough to capture stunning photos and videos.

4. Price: What’s Your Budget?

Apple’s Pro Max models come with a premium price tag, and the storage upgrades can make it even steeper. If budget constraints are a concern, the Pro provides nearly all the same features for less.

5. Weight and Handling: Do You Value Ergonomics?

With its larger size, the Pro Max is significantly heavier. If you spend hours scrolling, gaming, or texting, the added weight could become a nuisance over time. The Pro, being lighter, offers a more ergonomic experience for extended use.

6. Storage Needs: How Much Space Do You Really Need?

Both models start with the same storage options, but if you’re leaning toward the Pro Max, you might also be considering higher storage tiers for all that extra content. Think about your current storage usage and future needs before making your choice.

The Final Verdict: Pro or Pro Max?

Choosing between the Pro and Pro Max ultimately comes down to your lifestyle, usage habits, and priorities.

  • If you want a lightweight phone that’s easier to carry around and don’t mind slightly less battery life, the Pro is your go-to.
  • If you’re a power user who loves a bigger screen, extended battery life, and a slightly better camera, the Pro Max is worth the splurge.

Whichever you choose, you’re getting an incredible device that’s built to last. Now, go ahead and pick your perfect iPhone match!

posts.title: Oops: Top 4 Tech/Gadget Fails of 2024
posts.content:
2024 has been a thrilling year for tech enthusiasts, with innovations that pushed boundaries and redefined possibilities, and we have covered some of the best ones here. But not all products hit the mark. For every triumph, there were a few high-profile flops that left us scratching our heads or outright disappointed. Here’s a roundup of the top four tech and gadget fails of 2024, showing that even the biggest players in the industry sometimes miss the target.

1. Apple Vision Pro

When Apple unveiled the Vision Pro, expectations soared. This sleek augmented reality headset promised to revolutionize the way we interact with technology. But the excitement fizzled out post-launch.

At a whopping price point, the Vision Pro struggled to justify its cost with its limited practical use cases. While it showcased cutting-edge technology, most consumers found it impractical for daily use. This wasn’t just about the price—it was about value. Niche applications and an unclear target audience meant the product appealed to a very small segment of buyers. As demand underwhelmed, Apple reportedly had to slash production forecasts, cementing the Vision Pro as one of the year’s biggest disappointments.

2. Wearable AI: Humane AI Pin & Rabbit R1

2024 was supposed to be the year wearable AI took center stage. Instead, devices like the Humane AI Pin and Rabbit R1 fell flat.

The Humane AI Pin, hyped as a futuristic gadget to simplify life, came with a price tag and functionality that few found appealing. Its lack of practicality, coupled with underwhelming features, left consumers cold.

The Rabbit R1 didn’t fare any better. Critics and early adopters alike pointed out its exorbitant cost and minimal utility. While wearable AI is a promising concept, these two products highlighted just how difficult it is to deliver affordable, functional, and user-friendly devices in this space.

3. Apple Intelligence

Apple’s leap into the AI-driven services market with "Apple Intelligence" was a bold move—but it turned into a stumbling block for the tech giant.

Plagued by privacy concerns, Apple Intelligence faced heavy scrutiny over the data it collected and how it planned to use it. These concerns, paired with a clunky user experience riddled with technical hiccups, led to widespread dissatisfaction. For a company that prides itself on seamless design and user-centric innovation, Apple Intelligence felt like an uncharacteristic misstep. Sadly, it remains unavailable in many regions, with many of the features currently unavailable.

4. Xiaomi & Redmi 8MP Ultrawide Cameras

In an era where smartphone photography is advancing rapidly, Xiaomi and Redmi's decision feels out of touch, delivering lacklustre images that fail to meet even modest expectations.

2024 reminded us that even the biggest names in tech aren’t immune to failure. From Apple’s Vision Pro and Intelligence to wearable AI flops and disappointing smartphone cameras, these missteps highlight the challenges of innovation.

But here’s the silver lining: failures often lead to better products.
